title: Closed-federation PSK derivation contradicts the canonical GCP3 vector
description: Security/protocol review finding: PskFederation::derive_context hashes the configured PSK through the private LICHEN-GCP-PSK-MASTER-v1 SHA-512 construction and supplies only 16 digest bytes as the OSCORE master secret. The canonical gcp3_trust_models.json vector and spec say the complete configured PSK is the RFC 8613 OSCORE master secret; the Rust test labeled as that vector checks only IDs and never asserts PRK/traffic keys. Independent implementations using the vector derive different keys, so closed federation cannot authenticate/decrypt. Implement the specified exact master-secret semantics (or update/specify/regenerate every oracle if a deliberate profile change), and add fixed expected PRK/sender key/recipient key/common-IV assertions independent of the production derivation.
